name: Argo CD
summary: A Kubernetes GitOps controller that compares Git-defined application targets with live cluster state, renders manifests through configured tools, and drives synchronization while reporting health and operation status.

features.name: Git-defined application target state
features.description: Argo CD models an Application with a target state derived from a source repository and compares it with the live Kubernetes state.
features.benefits: Makes deployment intent versioned and reviewable in Git
features.costs: Repository content, rendering tools, and cluster observations can diverge from operator expectations

features.name: Application refresh and synchronization loop
features.description: The application controller refreshes comparisons, determines sync status, and performs sync operations that apply changes toward the target state.
features.benefits: Automates repeatable convergence and exposes operation status
features.costs: Retries, ordering, hooks, and partial failures create transient divergence

features.name: Health and revision-aware operations
features.description: Argo CD reports application health separately from sync status and retains operation/revision information for inspection and rollback-oriented workflows.
features.benefits: Separates configuration equality from runtime health
features.costs: Health checks are tool/resource-specific and a prior revision does not guarantee restoration of external state

mathematical_views.question: How do repository target state, rendered manifests, live observations, and sync actions form a feedback loop?
assumptions: Git is treated as the target-state source
The controller can observe live resources and issue idempotent operations
The model does not infer convergence time or success for every sync

mathematical_views.question: How are sync equality, operation status, and runtime health represented as distinct coordinates?
assumptions: Sync status compares target and live state
Health is evaluated independently of exact manifest equality
The view abstracts individual health checks

mathematical_views.question: Which application revisions and sync operations can be selected for deployment or rollback?
assumptions: Revisions identify source or rendered application versions
Operations may fail or be superseded
Rollback is modeled as selecting a prior revision, not as a proof of environmental reversal

costs: Git and rendering become critical dependencies
Eventual convergence and repeated operations require idempotent resources
Health semantics vary by resource and rollback has external-state limits
